d: any instrument or means of binding or tying; used for binding objects together or restraining prisoners
an instrument for joining together objects (normally two)
a thin piece of metal (usually iron) sharpened on one end (in the NT used only in connection with nails employed in the crucifixion)
leather strap or thong (used in binding sandals or shoes and as thongs in a whip)
a series of connected metal links; used for binding objects together or restraining prisoners
an instrument consisting of heavy blocks of wood through which the legs were placed and then securely fastened
metal chains with special links prepared to go around the ankles; used to restrict the movement of a prisoner

g: chain (made of metal) or rope (made of fiber)

d: thick cord formed by twisting or braiding several strands together; made of a variety of materials, including palm fibers, linen, or reeds
